note: Deep Research taxon database. Sizes are typical adult maxima in metres; ages in Ma.

taxa.name: Stromatolite
taxa.habit: laminated microbial buildup on warm shelves
taxa.note: The dominant reef of the first three billion years. Declines sharply in the Cambrian as grazing and burrowing begin; survives today only in refugia like Hamelin Pool.

taxa.name: Bangiomorpha
taxa.note: Among the oldest fossils showing sexual reproduction and complex multicellularity.

taxa.name: Acritarchs
taxa.note: Mostly the cysts of algae; the workhorse biostratigraphic fossil of the Proterozoic and early Palaeozoic.

taxa.name: Cryoconite communities
taxa.habit: meltponds on the surface of snowball ice
taxa.note: The best candidate refugium for photosynthetic life through the Sturtian and Marinoan glaciations.

taxa.name: Charnia
taxa.habit: sessile frond anchored by a holdfast, in the deep sea below the photic zone
taxa.note: The first complex macrofossil recognised from rocks then thought to be Precambrian.

taxa.name: Fractofusus
taxa.habit: reclining on the sea floor, deep water
taxa.note: Shows evidence of reproduction by stolons.

taxa.name: Dickinsonia
taxa.habit: flat on a microbial mat, possibly mobile
taxa.diet: external digestion of the mat beneath it
taxa.note: Cholesteroid biomarkers argue it was an animal. Up to 1.4 m and a few mm thick.

taxa.name: Kimberella
taxa.note: The strongest Ediacaran candidate for a bilaterian, possibly mollusc-like; leaves scratch traces beside its body fossils.

taxa.name: Yorgia
taxa.note: Found with a trail of its own feeding impressions.

taxa.name: Tribrachidium
taxa.note: A body plan with no counterpart in any living phylum.

taxa.name: Ernietta
taxa.habit: partly buried, sack-like, in shifting sand

taxa.name: Cloudina
taxa.note: One of the FIRST mineralised skeletons, and it carries the first evidence of predation: drill holes made by something that hunted it.

taxa.name: Anomalocaris
taxa.habit: active nektonic swimmer with lateral flaps
taxa.note: The largest Cambrian animal; compound eyes with tens of thousands of lenses.

taxa.name: Opabinia
taxa.diet: predator, using a single frontal grasping proboscis
taxa.note: Five eyes. Burgess Shale.

taxa.name: Hallucigenia
taxa.note: Reconstructed upside-down and back-to-front for decades.

taxa.name: Wiwaxia
taxa.habit: benthic, armoured with sclerites and spines

taxa.name: Marrella
taxa.habit: swimming and crawling near the bottom
taxa.note: The most abundant animal in the Burgess Shale.

taxa.name: Olenellus
taxa.note: Index fossil of Laurentia, Baltica and Siberia.

taxa.name: Redlichia
taxa.note: Index fossil of Gondwana and its margins.

taxa.name: Myllokunmingia
taxa.note: Among the earliest known craniates, from Chengjiang.

taxa.name: Archaeocyaths
taxa.habit: sessile, cup-shaped, reef-forming on tropical shelves
taxa.note: The FIRST animal reef builders. Extinct by the mid-Cambrian, leaving reef building to microbes again until the Ordovician.

taxa.name: Small shelly fauna
taxa.note: Spines, plates, tubes and caps 1-2 mm long; the bridge between the Ediacaran and the Lagerstatten.

taxa.name: Cameroceras
taxa.habit: nektonic, with a long straight conical shell
taxa.note: Among the largest animals of the early Palaeozoic; the classic figure of ~9 m is probably an overestimate.

taxa.name: Isotelus
taxa.note: One of the largest trilobites.

taxa.name: Didymograptus
taxa.note: Graptolites are the definitive Ordovician-Silurian biostratigraphic tool because they were planktonic and therefore near-global.

taxa.name: Halysites
taxa.note: Part of the stromatoporoid-tabulate-rugose reef that replaces the Cambrian archaeocyath and microbial mound.

taxa.name: Conodonts
taxa.note: Known for a century from their teeth alone; the animal was found only in 1983.

taxa.name: Cooksonia
taxa.habit: tiny dichotomising axes in damp lowlands
taxa.note: Among the first vascular plants; a few centimetres tall, with terminal sporangia.

taxa.name: Baragwanathia
taxa.habit: creeping and upright shoots with true microphylls

taxa.name: Aglaophyton
taxa.note: From the Rhynie chert, and the earliest clear evidence of arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis - land plants have always been partly fungal.

taxa.name: Prototaxites
taxa.habit: free-standing column, the tallest organism of its day
taxa.note: No modern analogue. For 130 Myr the largest organism on land was probably a fungus.

taxa.name: Archaeopteris
taxa.habit: the first true forest tree: real wood, roots to ~1 m, a spreading crown
taxa.note: Deep rooting and canopy shade begin the silicate-weathering and organic-burial drawdown of CO2 that ends in the Late Palaeozoic Ice Age.

taxa.name: Wattieza
taxa.note: Earliest known tree-form, from Gilboa.

taxa.name: Elkinsia
taxa.note: Among the earliest seed plants - the innovation that frees reproduction from standing water.

taxa.name: Dunkleosteus
taxa.habit: nektonic apex predator with bladed jaw plates instead of teeth
taxa.note: One of the highest bite forces measured for any fish.

taxa.name: Tiktaalik
taxa.habit: shallow-water predator with a mobile neck and weight-bearing fins
taxa.note: Found by predicting the ROCK first: Devonian, shallow-marine to freshwater, then searching Ellesmere Island.

taxa.name: Ichthyostega
taxa.habit: amphibious, with limbs but a fish-like tail
taxa.note: Seven toes.

taxa.name: Eurypterids
taxa.habit: nektobenthic, some in brackish and fresh water
taxa.note: Jaekelopterus at ~2.5 m is the largest arthropod that ever lived, rivalled only by Arthropleura.

taxa.name: Stringocephalus
taxa.note: A Middle Devonian index fossil of the Old World Realm.

taxa.name: Australocoelia
taxa.note: Diagnostic of the cold high-latitude Gondwanan realm.

taxa.name: Lepidodendron
taxa.habit: unbranched pole with a crown, DETERMINATE growth - grew, reproduced once, died
taxa.note: >50 m tall and 2 m across at the base, with a shallow stigmarian rooting system. This is the coal.

taxa.name: Sigillaria
taxa.habit: tall, usually unbranched, in coal swamps

taxa.name: Calamites
taxa.habit: clonal thickets on levees and channel margins
taxa.note: >10 m tall, with a unifacial vascular cambium - it made wood in a way no living plant does.

taxa.name: Medullosa
taxa.habit: scrambling or self-supporting, with very large fronds
taxa.note: Produced the largest pollen grains known.

taxa.name: Psaronius
taxa.habit: tree fern with a mantle of adventitious roots
taxa.note: Takes over the tropical wetlands after the ~305 Ma rainforest collapse.

taxa.name: Cordaites
taxa.habit: tree with strap-shaped leaves; coastal and upland
taxa.note: The dominant tree of the cool Angaran province, and a relative of conifers.

taxa.name: Arthropleura
taxa.note: The largest known land arthropod. Traditionally tied to high O2 and the coal forest, but recent work finds it after the collapse and probably forest-independent.

taxa.name: Meganeura
taxa.note: Same caveat as Arthropleura on the oxygen story.

taxa.name: Hylonomus
taxa.habit: insectivore living in hollow lycopsid stumps
taxa.note: Among the earliest amniotes - the group that could reproduce away from water and so inherited the drying world.

taxa.name: Eurydesma
taxa.habit: cold-water shelf, often in glacial dropstone facies
taxa.note: The diagnostic cold-water fauna of the Late Palaeozoic Ice Age in Gondwana.

taxa.name: Fusulinids
taxa.note: Grain-of-wheat shaped and up to 6 cm. Their PRESENCE marks the warm Tethyan realm and their ABSENCE marks the cool Gondwanan and Boreal ones.

taxa.name: Glossopteris
taxa.habit: woody tree in very wet soils, like a modern bald cypress; conical, widely spaced crowns to exploit low-angle polar light
taxa.note: Trunk to 80 cm, tongue-shaped leaves 2-30 cm with reticulate venation. Antarctic wood shows broad growth rings and an abrupt autumn shutdown taking as little as a month. Its distribution across five now-separated continents was Suess's evidence for Gondwana. Died out BEFORE 252.3 Ma, ~350 kyr ahead of the marine extinction.

taxa.name: Gangamopteris
taxa.habit: as Glossopteris but with non-midribbed leaves

taxa.name: Vertebraria
taxa.habit: septate, air-filled roots in waterlogged soil
taxa.note: The root of Glossopteris, named separately before the connection was known; its internal air channels are a waterlogging adaptation.

taxa.name: Gigantopteris
taxa.habit: climbing or scrambling, with large net-veined leaves
taxa.note: The marker of the everwet Cathaysian province, whose rainforest survives the Euramerican collapse and persists to the end-Permian.

taxa.name: Rufloria
taxa.habit: deciduous tree with strong growth rings
taxa.note: The characteristic Angaran leaf - cool temperate, seasonal, deciduous.

taxa.name: Dimetrodon
taxa.habit: terrestrial apex predator with a tall neural-spine sail
taxa.note: Not a dinosaur, and closer to us than to any reptile.

taxa.name: Inostrancevia
taxa.habit: terrestrial apex predator with sabre canines

taxa.name: Lystrosaurus
taxa.note: The type case of post-extinction cosmopolitanism: after the end-Permian it was briefly a large fraction of all land vertebrates, on every continent.

taxa.name: Helicoprion
taxa.habit: nektonic, with a spiral tooth whorl in the lower jaw

taxa.name: Dicroidium
taxa.note: Replaces Glossopteris across Gondwana after the end-Permian.

taxa.name: Pleuromeia
taxa.note: A disaster taxon: it carpets the early Triassic when the forests are gone.

taxa.name: Cynognathus
taxa.note: Its Gondwana-wide distribution was classic evidence for continental drift.

taxa.name: Eoraptor
taxa.note: From the Ischigualasto Formation, Argentina - near the base of the dinosaur radiation.

taxa.name: Araucaria
taxa.note: Still living - monkey puzzle and Norfolk Island pine are the same genus that dominated Jurassic forests.

taxa.name: Williamsonia
taxa.habit: stout trunk with a crown of pinnate leaves and flower-like cones
taxa.note: Bennettitales look like cycads and are not; their bisexual cones long confused the search for the origin of flowers.

taxa.name: Ginkgo
taxa.note: One species survives; the genus was near-global in the Jurassic and Cretaceous.

taxa.name: Brachiosaurus
taxa.habit: high browser with forelimbs longer than hindlimbs

taxa.name: Diplodocus
taxa.habit: low-to-mid browser with a whip tail

taxa.name: Stegosaurus
taxa.habit: low browser with dorsal plates and a spiked tail

taxa.name: Archaeopteryx
taxa.note: From the Solnhofen lagoon, a hypersaline lagoonal Lagerstatte whose fauna is a mixture of marine, terrestrial and aerial - which is why it should not be realm-locked in a biota panel.

taxa.name: Buchia
taxa.note: A diagnostic Boreal-realm marker.

taxa.name: Archaefructus
taxa.note: Among the oldest flowering plants with preserved reproductive structures, from the Yixian Formation.

taxa.name: Rudists
taxa.habit: sessile, conical, gregarious - a bivalve behaving like a coral
taxa.note: They displace corals as the main tropical reef builder for much of the Cretaceous, and die at the K-Pg.

taxa.name: Triceratops
taxa.habit: low browser with a frill and three horns

taxa.name: Quetzalcoatlus
taxa.habit: terrestrial stalker and soaring flier, ~11 m wingspan
taxa.note: Among the largest flying animals that ever lived.

taxa.name: Hesperornis
taxa.note: A bird, so it is realm 'air' by clade and 'sea' by ecology - a case where a strict realm lock produces the wrong answer.

taxa.name: Ammonites
taxa.note: The single most useful Mesozoic biostratigraphic group; gone at the K-Pg while nautiloids survived.

taxa.name: Coccolithophores
taxa.note: From ~201 Ma they rain carbonate onto the DEEP sea floor for the first time, moving the carbonate factory off the shelf and giving the modern ocean its clear blue colour.

taxa.name: Metasequoia
taxa.habit: deciduous canopy tree, forming high-latitude forests
taxa.note: Polar broadleaf-deciduous forest grew inside the Arctic Circle in the Eocene; Metasequoia is its signature. Described as a fossil in 1941 and found alive in 1944.

taxa.name: Nothofagus
taxa.habit: canopy tree of cool temperate rainforest
taxa.note: Its distribution across South America, New Zealand, Australia and (fossil) Antarctica is a Gondwanan vicariance pattern.

taxa.name: Titanoboa
taxa.note: Its size implies a mean annual temperature above ~30 C in Palaeocene Colombia.

taxa.name: Basilosaurus
taxa.habit: fully aquatic, serpentine, with vestigial hindlimbs
taxa.note: A whale still carrying the legs of its land ancestry.

taxa.name: Uintatherium
taxa.habit: heavy browser with six blunt horns

taxa.name: Nummulites
taxa.note: Coin-sized single cells; the limestone of the Egyptian pyramids is largely made of them.

taxa.name: Andropogoneae
taxa.note: C4 grasslands expand in the late Miocene (~8 Ma) under low CO2 and seasonal aridity - the biome that makes the modern savanna fauna possible.

taxa.name: Proconsul
taxa.note: ENDEMIC TO AFRICA. Its appearance on an Australian-sector card was the bug that exposed the endemism filter not reaching submerged and island labels.

taxa.name: Megatherium
taxa.habit: terrestrial browser, able to rear on its hindlimbs
taxa.note: A South American native that invaded North America during the Great American Interchange, in one of at least eight ground-sloth lineages to do so.

taxa.name: Phorusrhacids
taxa.note: Apex predators of isolated South America; possibly island-hopped north by ~5 Ma.

taxa.name: Toxodon
taxa.habit: heavy grazer, rhinoceros-like in build but unrelated
taxa.note: One of the endemic South American ungulate orders that the interchange extinguished.

taxa.name: Mammuthus primigenius
taxa.habit: cold-adapted grazer of the mammoth steppe
taxa.note: The mammoth steppe - cold, dry, productive grassland - is a biome with no modern equivalent, and it vanished with the ice.

taxa.name: Homo sapiens
taxa.note: Cited as pivotal in the late Pleistocene megafaunal extinctions on every continent it reached.

taxa.name: Rhizophora
taxa.habit: intertidal tree on stilt roots, salt-excluding
taxa.note: Mangrove is the one forest that shows up as coastline rather than as interior vegetation, and it is a Cenozoic feature.

taxa.name: Diatoms
taxa.note: Radiate strongly from the Cretaceous and dominate high-latitude and upwelling productivity in the Cenozoic; they draw silica down and are why sponges and radiolarians build thinner skeletons than they used to.

taxa.name: Haikouichthys
taxa.habit: nektonic, with a skull and rudimentary vertebral elements
taxa.note: From Chengjiang: among the oldest known vertebrates.

taxa.name: Aysheaia
taxa.habit: benthic, walked on lobopods among sponges

taxa.name: Promissum
taxa.habit: nektonic, eel-like with phosphatic feeding elements
taxa.note: A giant conodont from the Soom Shale, deposited under the Hirnantian ice.

taxa.name: Sacabambaspis
taxa.note: An early armoured jawless fish from Gondwana - the vertebrates arrive in shallow water on the southern continent, not the tropics.

taxa.name: Aegirocassis
taxa.note: The Ordovician turns the Cambrian's apex predator lineage into a whale-shark analogue: the same appendages, remodelled into a plankton net.

taxa.name: Pterygotus
taxa.habit: nektonic sea scorpion with crushing chelicerae
taxa.note: Eurypterids are the largest arthropods that ever lived and they dominate Silurian shelf predation before jawed fish take it over.
